name: killall
description: Kills processes by exact command name (not pattern) — simpler than pkill but less flexible.

flags.description: Send SIGTERM to every process whose name matches exactly.
Ask for confirmation for each process.

examples.explanation: Terminates all processes literally named firefox.
Interactive mode: confirms each match, protecting you from killing your own shell.

about: killall matches the exact name (no regex, unlike pkill) and comes from the psmisc package. On some Unix systems (Solaris, older System V) killall is a DIFFERENT, dangerous command that shuts down all processes — do not assume portability.
useCases: Stop all instances of a known program.
mistakes: Expecting regex or partial matches — names must match exactly.
Using killall on non-Linux Unix systems where it has a different meaning.
warnings: killall bash can kill your own shell. Use -i when unsure.
